rationale:
MEASURED IN PRODUCTION 2026-08-23: 15 of 49 copy_gate markers with `targets > 0` do not reconcile — `targets != len(rewritten) + len(rejected)` — and 12 of those account for NONE of their targets. Query: over orchestration_states, jsonb_each on collected_data, keys LIKE 'copy_gate%' with status='repaired' and targets>0.

THE CAUSE IS STRUCTURAL, NOT OCCASIONAL, and it is one line of control flow: runNegationRepair's accept/reject loop iterates `decodeReplacements(parsed)` — the MODEL'S answer — not `plan.targets`. Every branch INSIDE the loop appends to rewritten or rejected, so the accounting is complete for everything the model mentions; a target the answer never mentions is visited by no branch at all and is recorded nowhere. First-hand verification substituted for a 090 run (owner ruling 2026-07-31): the claim is local and self-evidencing — the loop header names its own range expression, the census quantifies the consequence, and a mutation reproduces it on demand.

WHY IT MATTERS EVEN THOUGH NO PAGE WAS EVER MISDESCRIBED. `hits_after` is recomputed from the real content and stayed honest throughout, so this never made a false claim about an artefact. What it corrupted is the INSTRUMENT. This action's entire displacement defence is that it fails CLOSED and records every rejection with its reason — the file's own header says that log 'is how we find out whether the repair is fixing the copy or teaching the model a new tic'. And bugs_open/305's open decision D3 (is `rather than` a tic or ordinary English? it is in 43% of writer sections) is explicitly to be settled FROM that log after a week of traffic. So an unreconciled 31% was about to inform an owner decision while looking complete.

THE FIX records every unanswered target as a rejection with reason `no_answer_for_target`, so the invariant `targets == rewritten + rejected` holds for every marker and a census can distinguish 'the model declined this shape' from 'the model never addressed it'. It is deliberately NOT a failure: the copy stands as written exactly as for any other rejection, and hits_after already said so.

plan.summary: Close a silent accounting hole in the copy gate's repair log. The accept/reject loop iterates the model's replacements, so a target the model ignores is recorded in neither list — measured at 15 of 49 markers, 12 of them accounting for no targets at all. The fix tracks which targets were answered and records the rest as rejections with reason `no_answer_for_target`, making `targets == rewritten + rejected` hold. No page was ever misdescribed (hits_after is recomputed from real content); the damage was to the log that an open owner decision (D3) is to be settled from. Accounting extracted into a pure helper so the invariant is directly testable; three properties mutation-proven, including one test added only because a mutation PASSED.

edits.rationale: Track which targets the model actually answered, keyed the same way matchTarget matches, and append the remainder after the loop. The comment states the control-flow reason (the loop ranges over the answer, not the ask) because that is what makes the bug invisible on inspection.

A pure helper so the invariant can be tested without an AI client — the existing tests in this file mimic the loop for exactly that reason. negationTargetKey normalises the sentence so a target that WAS answered is not re-reported as ignored on a curly apostrophe, and NUL-separates field from sentence so `field+sentence` cannot be ambiguous.

Three tests, each mutation-proven. The third exists ONLY because a mutation passed: removing the NUL separator broke nothing, so the comment claiming it guards a collision was unenforced. A protection no test exercises is not a protection.

grounded_in: rewrite_negations_action.go header, the action's own stated defence: 'AcceptNegationRewrite fails CLOSED and every rejection is recorded with its reason. That log is the instrument: it is how we find out whether the repair is fixing the copy or teaching the model a new tic.'
bugs_open/305 D3, an OPEN OWNER DECISION resting on that log: 'It is in 43% of writer sections... The rejection log after a week of traffic informs this; the call is taste, and taste is the owner's.'
CENSUS [MEASURED 2026-08-23]: markers with targets>0 = 49; reconciling = 34; NOT reconciling = 15; of those, accounting for zero targets = 12. Live orchestration_states, all history of the gate.

WORKED CASE, live the same morning: ai-agent-orchestration.com/protocol-tracker (10:49Z) — copy_gate_0 targets=1 rewritten=1; copy_gate_1 targets=1 rejected=1; copy_gate_2 targets=1 rewritten=0 rejected=0. The third is the hole, in a run whose other two iterations account correctly.

MUTATION EVIDENCE 2026-08-23: (1) neutralising the unanswered loop fails TestEveryTargetIsAccountedFor... with 'unanswered targets = 0, want 2'; (2) dropping normaliseSentenceKey from the key fails the punctuation test; (3) dropping the NUL separator PASSED the whole suite until a collision test was added for it, which then fails with 'two distinct targets share a key ("abc is not d.")'.

NOT A BEHAVIOUR CHANGE TO ANY PAGE: hits_after is recomputed by countNegationHits over the real content map, independently of these lists, so no marker's claim about copy changes. Only the rejected[] array grows.
plan.risks:
MARKER SIZE: rejected[] gains one entry per unanswered target, each carrying a 160-char `from`. Markers are persisted in orchestration_states.collected_data; on the measured corpus this adds at most a handful of entries per section, but a reviewer should confirm no consumer assumes rejected[] is small or that every entry carries `to` (the unanswered shape deliberately has no `to`, since no replacement was proposed — a consumer indexing r['to'] blindly would now see nil more often).
SEMANTIC: `no_answer_for_target` is a rejection in the accounting sense but NOT a judgement — the model did not decline it, it never addressed it. Anyone computing a 'rejection rate' as a quality signal must exclude this reason or the rate silently mixes two different events. That is the main thing worth pressing on, and it is why the reason string is distinct rather than reusing an existing one.
SCOPE: confined to one action; no config key, no ActionInputSpec change, so the RFC_022 optional-key budget is unaffected. Verified against clean HEAD in a git-archive tree because another session's uncommitted work currently breaks `go build ./...` in the shared tree (unrelated files: render_site_components_action.go, section_editor_actions.go).
